title: 3_Parametric Form

findings.finding: The topic has no opening review of linear rearrangement and bracket expansion, which its worked examples use directly.
findings.breakdown: Students must rearrange x=3t+1, isolate y in a linear equation, and expand a squared binomial while learning parameter conversion. Incorrectly omitting the cross term in (2t-2)^2 changes the resulting curve.
findings.checked: The complete supplied teaching contains no earlier topic or opening review. These algebraic operations are substantial steps in the worked examples. Signed substitution was removed from the finding because the cited negative-value calculations occur in the opening investigation rather than a worked example. The topic's conversion instructions explain substitution and elimination, but do not independently rehearse the underlying algebra.
findings.assumptions: Linear rearrangement and binomial expansion are prior Stage 6 knowledge. No calculator assumption is needed.

repair.proposal: Insert three short review items before p3-sketching-block: (a) Make t the subject of x=3t+1. Answer: t=(x-1)/3. (b) Make y the subject of 5x-2y+10=0. Answer: y=(5x+10)/2. (c) Expand and simplify (2u-1)^2+3(2u-1)-1. Answer: 4u^2+2u-3. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: The opening review rehearses linear rearrangement and bracket expansion before the worked conversions use them.

findings.finding: Extend Question 9 by comparing the parabola segments traced by adjacent parameter intervals.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up connects the parameter interval to the portion of the Cartesian curve represented.
findings.checked: Eliminating t gives y=3-2(x-2)^2. For 0≤t≤1, x ranges from 2 to 3 and the endpoints are (2,3) and (3,1). For -1≤t≤1, the domain and range are both [1,3]. Each proposed part asks one question and uses the existing equations.
findings.assumptions: Uses the substitution, plotting and Cartesian conversion methods supplied in this topic, together with prior domain-and-range knowledge.

repair.proposal: After p9-q9-root add: (b) Sketch the curve for the same equations when 0≤t≤1, labelling its endpoints. Answer: y=3-2(x-2)^2 for 2≤x≤3, with endpoints (2,3) and (3,1). (c) State the domain and range when -1≤t≤1. Answer: domain [1,3], range [1,3].

findings.doneWhen: The follow-up compares parameter intervals while retaining the original equations.

findings.finding: Extend the existing circle question by restricting its parameter to trace a semicircle.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up distinguishes the complete Cartesian circle from the portion traced over a restricted parameter interval.
findings.checked: For x=1+2cosθ and y=-3+2sinθ, θ=0 gives (3,-3) and θ=π gives (-1,-3). Since sinθ≥0 on [0,π], the trace is exactly the upper semicircle, including both endpoints. The circle methods and earlier restricted-parameter question supply the required methods; the proposed dependence on p15-q7 is unnecessary.
findings.assumptions: Stage 6 students have prior unit-circle trigonometry and radian knowledge, consistent with the circle investigation.

repair.proposal: After p13-q3b add: (c) For the same equations with 0≤θ≤π, state the endpoints of the curve. Answer: (3,-3) and (-1,-3). (d) Sketch the part traced over this interval. Answer: the upper semicircle of (x-1)^2+(y+3)^2=4, with y≥-3, including both endpoints.

findings.doneWhen: The follow-up identifies and sketches the restricted trace of the existing circle.

protectedGroups.observation: Changing the radius changes the right-hand side of the Cartesian equation to its square.
protectedGroups.invariant: Origin-centred circle, trigonometric coordinate assignment and conversion steps.
